title: I finally released A Starcrossed Limbo: The Darkest Timeline; a massive, dark fantasy RPG 10+ years in the making
author: Accurate_Moment_9883
selftext:
I just released A Starcrossed Limbo: The Darkest Timeline on [itch.io](http://itch.io) after working on this world and story for more than ten years.  
  
This was a game I began making with a close friend over ten years ago and kept chipping away at over the last decade, with endless lore, stories, and scattered words. Now AI is finally advanced and accessible enough that, even without infinite resources, bringing all of it to reality was possible within my lifetime.  
  
It wouldn't exist without an AI system I built specifically to survive making it, nor would it exist by simply throwing prompts at an LLM.  
  
For the last 17 years, and especially the last four, I built an AI system I call Harmony, wired directly into my life and my 4090s.  
  
Together we spent over a hundred billion tokens wrestling 700+ maps, custom plugins, painted environments, battle systems, and a world-decay sanity mechanic called Grey Static.  
  
Half the systems and encounters in this game were argued over, audited, broken, and fixed line by line between us in the middle of the night.  
  
As for the game itself, here's the short version:  
  
What came out the other side is a 70+ hour, unforgiving dark-fantasy RPG that is, from my perspective, the closest thing to a complete 2D RPG that could be made by a single person.  
The beginning and summary are simple.  
  
You start at a small fire on the edge of Nothing with Dark Admiral Rats and his comrade named Dont.  
  
The game is sprawling and open-ended, with non-linear world and level design. There are no levels, no XP grinding, no random encounters, and nobody holding your hand; just 10 companions, 7+ endings, and a world that literally drains its own color and warps the UI if you push too long without resting.  
  
For a long while I wasn't sure I could carry something this massive all the way to release without burning out or gutting it.  
While my close friend didn't live long enough to see its release, and I'd been content just keeping it to myself forever, I decided to release it in the end.  
  
If anyone's dumb enough to buy it or take a further look at it, you can buy it or read more about it here.  
  
Windows, $14.20 (Steam targeting December 4th):  
[https://staronline7.itch.io/a-starcrossed-limbo-the-darkest-timeline](https://staronline7.itch.io/a-starcrossed-limbo-the-darkest-timeline)

replies.author: Accurate_Moment_9883
replies.body:
I can give you a spoiler free short version.  
  
I spent a lot of time on the game but even more time on the story. This is 100% a story game first.  
  
Basically two "idiots", trying to escape an inescapable Limbo. Rats desperately wants to live and find freedom, while Dont is pretty damn tired of existing forever.  
They start at a little campfire on the edge of Nothing, and what follows is a sprawling journey through a very strange world as they uncover what Limbo actually is and find a way to escape a never ending limbo.  
It's dark fantasy with a lot of existential horror, and themes of comradery, justice and freedom.  
The story can go in some wildly different directions depending on what you discover, there's a lot of endings.  
The story is open-ended in a way that rewards you paying attention. It tries to deceive you.  
  
If you like chrono trigger, there is timelines involved, a zero railroaded story, that lets you build your own path each time, with an ending based on your decisions.  
  
I could compare it very loosely to a movie called "Primer" even though it is completely different in execution.  
  
I'm biased, so I think the story is incredible, it's the whole reason I made the game.

replies.author: Accurate_Moment_9883
replies.body:
Since we're making accusations about licensing, here's Yanfly's actual statement:

[https://yanfly.moe/wiki/Official\_Statement\_from\_Yanfly\_Regarding\_Porting\_of\_Plugins](https://yanfly.moe/wiki/Official_Statement_from_Yanfly_Regarding_Porting_of_Plugins)

And the official terms:

[https://yanfly.moe/wiki/Category:Yanfly\_Engine\_Plugins#Terms\_of\_Use](https://yanfly.moe/wiki/Category:Yanfly_Engine_Plugins#Terms_of_Use)

Yanfly explicitly permits using original MV plugins in commercial RPG Maker games, including making compatibility edits for MZ, provided the credits are retained and the modified plugins aren't redistributed outside the game.

Darkest Timeline is (now was) an RPG Maker MZ game using Fossil for compatibility, not a standalone redistribution of Yanfly plugins. Yanfly is credited, and the remaining dependencies are being replaced regardless.

You could have read the actual license before accusing me of theft.

comments.author: AsparagusOk8818
comments.body:
This is just wild in terms of the theft and brazen lies about inventing some revolutionary system. This is just stolen work from RPGMaker and the RPGMaker community, particularly Yanfly's plugins.

...It'll be interesting to see where this kind of crap goes. The RTP is all copyrighted... but I don't THINK you technically are straying outside of the ToS if you port the RTP to a different engine? At the time it was made, that would've been such a crazy prospect that probably the ToS didn't bother covering it. 

Yanfly would be appalled at the idea of having his plugins ripped like this, though. 

  
I'd be shocked if this... erm... 'project' took more than a week to put together. It looks worse than a proof of concept I slapped together ages ago in RPGMaker, and that took maybe a month? And I had no AI help. 

  
Anyone who doesn't know the RPGMaker RTP, though, or Yanfly's work could easily be tricked into believing the work is original. And since the assets are hand drawn (albeit hand drawn for the community), they don't even need to be disclosed as AI and you can argue that stealing them isn't TECHNICALLY theft since, hey, they were offered for free! Kind of like scooping the coins out of a donation box and pocketing them, or raiding the local charity clothing bin for stuff to resell.

comments.author: Accurate_Moment_9883
comments.body:
It's pretty wild watching people make confident claims about a game they haven't even played.

I built Darkest Timeline primarily for myself and a friend. I'm a solo developer, and I have nothing to lose by releasing it. If people enjoy it, fantastic. If nobody plays it, I still made the game I wanted to make.

Hand-drawing every asset at this scale simply wasn't feasible. Some assets are hand-drawn, others aren't. Most went from my own sketches through a custom local LoRA and then GPT Image. The available tools have evolved enormously in just the last few months.

And the plugin argument is particularly strange. We're at a point where Yanfly-adjacent functionality can be recreated, extended, or improved in under 30 minutes with modern tools.

I figured a community called r/aigamedev would be interested in what a solo developer can actually accomplish with these tools.

Apparently some people would rather invent claims about a game they've never touched.

Hilarious.
